standard_text: Energy is found in different forms, is conserved, and has the ability to do work: work, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy, power and efficiency, and thermal energy and specific heat. body_html:
How to think about it

Work is done when a force moves an object: W = Fd (in joules). Kinetic energy is ½mv² and gravitational potential energy is mgh. With no friction, mechanical energy is conserved. Power is P = W ÷ t (in watts) and efficiency = useful output ÷ input × 100%.

Thermal energy depends on temperature and mass. The heat needed to change temperature is Q = mcΔT, where c is the specific heat capacity (water: 4.18 J/g·°C).

Example

How much work is done pushing a box 3.0 m with 50 N?

W = Fd

Answer: 150 J

Example

How much heat raises 100 g of water by 10 °C?

Q = mcΔT = 100 × 4.18 × 10

Answer: 4,180 J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking work is done when nothing moves.
  • Forgetting to square v in kinetic energy.
  • Mixing up heat and temperature.

items.q: A gas absorbs 400 J of heat and does 250 J of work on its surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?
items.e: First law: ΔU = Q − W = 150 J.

items.q: How does heat spread through the air in a room from a heater?

items.q: Why does a wetsuit keep a surfer warm?

items.q: Why does the temperature stay constant while ice is melting?
c: the energy supplied breaks bonds (increases potential energy) rather than speeding up particles
items.e: This energy is the latent heat of fusion.

items.q: What is heat?
c: energy transferred because of a temperature difference
the total energy in an object
the temperature of a hot object
items.e: Heat flows from hot to cold.

items.q: What is the first law of thermodynamics?
c: temperature can never reach absolute zero
the change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done by the system (ΔU = Q − W)
heat always flows from cold to hot
energy is lost in every change

items.q: A gas absorbs 700 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?
items.e: First law: ΔU = Q − W = 500 J.

items.q: What is internal energy?
